title: Our mighty mother
html_source:
This could mean “the sea” – the ladies are coming down to the beach by the sea or it could mean “nature” – the ladies are coming down from the road into nature.

Echoes a phrase of AE Russell who defines the mighty mother as ‘nature in it’s spiritual aspect’ (Gifford p15).

BillGibbons suggests that because the reference to “Algy” earlier in the sentence refers to Algernon Charles Swinburne, it may follow that “our mighty mother” refers to the phrase “the great sweet mother” from Swinburne’s poem “The Triumph of Time.” If that is true, then “our mighty mother” undoubtedly means “the sea.”
